rules.sentence: Sjögren syndrome is a systemic autoimmune disease most commonly characterized by sicca symptoms—dry eyes and dry mouth—resulting from immune-mediated inflammation of the lacrimal and salivary glands.
In addition to glandular dysfunction, up to 50% of patients develop extraglandular involvement affecting the skin, lungs, kidneys, joints, and nervous system.

This activity for healthcare professionals is designed to enhance the learner's competence in identifying Sjögren syndrome, performing the recommended evaluation, and implementing an appropriate interprofessional approach when managing this condition to improve patient outcomes through earlier recognition, accurate diagnosis, and individualized management of this often-overlooked autoimmune disorder.
This course will provide clinicians with an in-depth understanding of the pathophysiology, clinical features, and diagnostic approach to Sjögren syndrome.

Emphasis will be placed on recognizing systemic complications, interpreting serologic and biopsy findings, utilizing validated diagnostic tools, and initiating individualized management strategies for both glandular and systemic disease, including emerging diagnostic technologies.
